title: Reading Practice 1 - The History of Tea
description: IELTS Academic Reading practice test about the history and cultural significance of tea.

stimuli.title: Passage 1: The History of Tea
stimuli.content:
A Tea is the most widely consumed beverage in the world after water, and its history stretches back nearly 5,000 years. According to Chinese legend, tea was discovered in 2737 BCE by Emperor Shen Nung when dried leaves from a wild tea tree blew into his pot of boiling water. He found the resulting drink refreshing and restorative. Although this legend is almost certainly apocryphal, archaeological evidence suggests that tea was being consumed in China as early as the second century BCE.

B For centuries, tea remained a Chinese secret. It was during the Tang Dynasty (618–907 CE) that tea drinking became widespread among all classes of Chinese society. Lu Yu, often called the "Sage of Tea," wrote the first comprehensive treatise on tea, the Cha Jing (The Classic of Tea), around 760 CE. This work covered everything from the cultivation of tea plants to the preparation and drinking of tea, and it helped elevate tea from a mere beverage to an art form. The Tang Dynasty also saw tea spread to Japan, where it would eventually give rise to the elaborate Japanese tea ceremony.

C Tea first reached Europe in the early 17th century, brought by Portuguese and Dutch traders. Initially, it was extremely expensive and consumed only by the wealthy elite. In England, tea became fashionable after Catherine of Braganza, the Portuguese wife of King Charles II, introduced it to the English court in 1662. By the 18th century, tea had become Britain's national drink, consumed by people of all social classes. The British East India Company held a virtual monopoly on the tea trade, importing vast quantities from China.

D The importance of tea in British culture led to one of the most significant events in world history: the Boston Tea Party of 1773. American colonists, angry at being taxed on tea by the British Parliament without having any representation, dumped an entire shipment of tea into Boston Harbor. This act of defiance was a catalyst for the American Revolution. Thus, a simple beverage played a pivotal role in the birth of a nation.

E In the 19th century, the British Empire sought to break China's monopoly on tea production by establishing tea plantations in India and Sri Lanka (then Ceylon). Robert Fortune, a Scottish botanist, was sent on a secret mission to China in 1848 to steal tea plants and the secrets of tea production. His mission was successful, and within a few decades, India had become the world's largest tea producer. The tea plantations of Darjeeling and Assam became famous for producing distinctive varieties of black tea.

F Today, tea is grown in more than 50 countries, and global production exceeds 6 million tonnes annually. China has reclaimed its position as the world's largest producer, followed by India, Kenya, and Sri Lanka. The tea industry employs millions of people worldwide, though it has faced criticism for poor working conditions on some plantations. Modern research has also highlighted numerous health benefits associated with tea consumption, including reduced risk of heart disease, certain cancers, and neurodegenerative conditions. From its legendary origins in ancient China to its current status as a global commodity, tea continues to shape cultures and economies around the world.

questionGroups.instruction: Questions 1-5: The reading passage has six paragraphs, A-F. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-F.

questions.content: A reference to the health advantages of drinking tea
Details of how tea was used as a form of political protest
A description of a book that transformed the perception of tea
An explanation of how a spy mission changed the tea industry
A mention of an unverified story about the origins of tea

questionGroups.instruction: Questions 6-9: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.content: Tea was initially affordable for all Europeans when it first arrived.
Lu Yu's book only discussed how to prepare and drink tea.
Robert Fortune learned to speak Chinese fluently before his mission.
India is currently the world's largest tea producer.

questionGroups.instruction: Questions 10-13: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

questions.content: According to the passage, when was tea first consumed in China?

options.label: C
options.content: As early as the second century BCE

questions.content: What role did Catherine of Braganza play in the history of tea?

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

options.label: B

options.label: D
